correctness.rationale: In A=F_q Q/J², idempotency forces each vertex coefficient to 0 or 1, every loop coefficient to zero, and independent off-diagonal radical coefficients only where the two incident vertex labels disagree. Consequently T_Q=∑_epsilon q^(crossing-arrow multiplicity). For d idempotents, diagonal evaluations separate vertices iff their d-bit label words are injective. The corner map U_ij:F_q^d→e_iJe_j generated by the chosen radical coordinates contributes surjectively to B∩J exactly when its restriction to the hyperplane ker Delta_ij is onto; the necessity follows by polynomial word telescoping, sufficiency by commutators and diagonal projectors (sandwiched into corners). On h disagreement positions the restriction has dimension h−1, giving q^m R_q(h−1,m) choices; all corners independent and loop presence prevents generation. This proves exact E_d and threshold h≥m+1, including all finite fields and zero-arrow cases. Independently enumerated full generated unital subalgebras over F2 for one arrow and two parallel/opposing arrows, reproducing respectively 8,0,16 generating idempotent pairs. Coding bound for M=1 follows from parity bipartition/matching in hypercube.

originality.rationale: Hu–Xiao proves the existence of some idempotent generators in qualitative module terms; Rowen–Segev constrains algebras generated by two idempotents; Sercombe–Shalev treats unrestricted finite associative algebra random generation. These do not give uniform-on-idempotents ordered-tuple probabilities, the exact Hamming-surjection law, or optimal d as a binary code-size constraint. The underlying block criterion and binary code bounds are established principles and not claimed as new. A previously unnoticed conditional enumeration remains possible.

The theorem is for split radical-square-zero quotients and unital generation; not higher radical powers.

value.rationale: Probability of generation by uniformly selected idempotents and minimal idempotent-generator number are natural finite-algebra invariants. The complete oriented-quiver formula covers arbitrary arrow multiplicities and finite field sizes; it translates existence sharply into error-correcting-code capacity and detects orientation that total idempotent counts miss. The quantitative conditional census goes beyond a mechanical substitution into unconditioned random generation.
